words.enDefinition: a document describing what a job involves

examples.en: The job description says I'll spend half my time helping visitors find their way around.
examples.zh: 「岗位说明」写着，我有一半时间要帮来访者找路。

examples.en: I downloaded the job description before asking my tutor what the position would involve.
examples.zh: 我下载了「岗位说明」，才去问导师这个职位具体做些什么。

words.enDefinition: a short summary of a job's main purpose

examples.en: The role overview made it clear that most of the work was done off campus.
examples.zh: 「岗位概览」写得很清楚，大部分工作在校外做。

examples.en: I read the role overview to see whether the job involved working with children.
examples.zh: 我读了「岗位概览」，看看这份工作是否需要和孩子打交道。

words.enDefinition: a document listing the qualities and qualifications needed for a role

examples.en: The UK charity attached a person specification listing the skills it expected applicants to have.
examples.zh: 这家英国慈善机构附了份「任职条件说明」，列出对申请人技能的要求。

examples.en: I printed the person specification and marked the requirements that were unclear to me.
examples.zh: 我打印了「任职条件说明」，标记了自己没弄懂的要求。

words.enDefinition: the name an organization gives to a particular job

examples.en: The job title sounded technical, but the duties were mostly helping visitors and answering phones.
examples.zh: 「职位名称」听起来很专业，但主要工作是接待来访者和接电话。

examples.en: I wrote down the job title because the library was hiring for two similar positions.
examples.zh: 图书馆在招两个很相似的岗位，所以我记下了这个「职位名称」。

words.enDefinition: a job intended for someone new to a field

examples.en: I'm looking for an entry-level position where my experience as a student volunteer will count.
examples.zh: 我在找一个「入门级岗位」，希望自己的学生志愿者经历能派上用场。

examples.en: The university advertised an entry-level position that was open to people changing careers too.
examples.zh: 学校招聘一个「入门级岗位」，转行的人也能申请。

words.enDefinition: a job between junior and senior levels of responsibility

examples.en: I realised it was a mid-level position when I saw the experience they expected.
examples.zh: 看到他们要求的工作经验后，我才意识到这是个「中级岗位」。

examples.en: The mid-level position involved running small projects with support from a senior coordinator.
examples.zh: 这个「中级岗位」要在资深协调员的支持下负责小项目。

collocations: a mid-level position in the team

words.enDefinition: a job demanding a high level of experience or responsibility

examples.en: The senior position included reviewing budgets and making decisions about which projects would go ahead.
examples.zh: 这个「高级岗位」要审核预算，还要决定哪些项目可以推进。

examples.en: I hadn't realised how much experience the senior position called for until I read the listing.
examples.zh: 看完招聘启事，我才知道这个「高级岗位」需要这么多经验。

collocations: a senior position in the department

words.enDefinition: a job offered without a set end date

examples.en: The museum listed one permanent position and two temporary jobs for summer visitors.
examples.zh: 博物馆发布了一个「长期岗位」，还有两个为夏季游客提供服务的临时岗位。

examples.en: I'm looking for a permanent position because my current contract ends next month.
examples.zh: 我在找「长期岗位」，因为现在的合同下个月就到期。

words.enDefinition: a job intended to last a limited time

examples.en: The library advertised a temporary position to cover staff leave during the exam period.
examples.zh: 图书馆招了一个「临时岗位」，在考试期间顶替休假的员工。

examples.en: A temporary position would suit me because I'm spending next semester at another university.
examples.zh: 我下学期要去另一所学校，所以「临时岗位」挺适合我。

words.enDefinition: an employment agreement for a specified length of time

examples.en: The archive offered a fixed-term contract that would run until the end of August.
examples.zh: 档案馆提供了一份「固定期限合同」，到八月底结束。

examples.en: I checked whether the fixed-term contract would finish before my next placement began.
examples.zh: 我查了一下这份「固定期限合同」会不会在下一段实习开始前结束。

words.enDefinition: work available during a particular time of year

examples.en: I did seasonal work at a visitor centre between the end of exams and September.
examples.zh: 我考完试到九月份之间，在游客中心做了份「季节性工作」。

examples.en: The shop offers seasonal work when it needs extra staff during the winter holidays.
examples.zh: 冬季假期需要更多人手时，这家商店会招人做「季节性工作」。

words.zhGloss: 无持续聘用承诺的用工
words.enDefinition: an Australian employment category without a guarantee of ongoing work
acceptedZhAnswers: 无持续聘用承诺的用工

examples.en: The Australian stadium advertised casual employment for people who could take shifts on match days.
examples.zh: 澳大利亚这家体育场招能在比赛日上班的员工，采用「无持续聘用承诺的用工」。

examples.en: At the Australian museum, I asked how shifts were offered under its casual employment arrangement.
examples.zh: 我在澳大利亚那家博物馆问了，这种「无持续聘用承诺的用工」是怎么安排班次的。

words.enDefinition: a job with the employer's usual full working hours

examples.en: The lab advertised a full-time position that would be difficult to fit around my classes.
examples.zh: 实验室招了个「全职岗位」，我很难兼顾上课和工作。

examples.en: I'm interested in the full-time position once my current course finishes in July.
examples.zh: 我的课程七月结束，之后我对这个「全职岗位」有兴趣。

words.enDefinition: a job with fewer hours than a full-time one

examples.en: I saw a part-time position at the campus café that fits around my Tuesday lectures.
examples.zh: 我看到学校咖啡馆在招「兼职岗位」，工作时间和周二的课不冲突。

examples.en: The arts centre offered a part-time position for two afternoons and one evening each week.
examples.zh: 艺术中心提供了一个「兼职岗位」，每周上两个下午和一个晚上的班。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement where two people share one job

examples.en: The listing offered a job share with someone already working on Thursdays and Fridays.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着可以「两人分担一个岗位」，另一位员工固定在每周四和周五上班。

examples.en: I asked whether a job share would be possible during my final year.
examples.zh: 我问自己上最后一年学时，能不能和别人「分担一个岗位」。

words.enDefinition: a job done away from the employer's workplace

examples.en: The remote position would let me work from home once I finished the training.
examples.zh: 培训结束后，这个「远程办公岗位」允许我居家工作。

examples.en: I checked the hours because the remote position was based in a different time zone.
examples.zh: 我查了工作时间，因为这个「远程办公岗位」的团队在另一个时区。

words.enDefinition: a job combining workplace attendance and remote work

examples.en: The hybrid role needs someone in the office twice a week and online otherwise.
examples.zh: 这个「混合办公岗位」每周要到办公室两次，其余时间在线工作。

examples.en: I asked which days the team came in before applying for the hybrid role.
examples.zh: 申请这个「混合办公岗位」之前，我问了团队一般哪几天到办公室。

collocations: a hybrid role with office days

words.enDefinition: a job carried out at a specified workplace

examples.en: The gallery described it as an on-site role because most duties involve greeting visitors.
examples.zh: 美术馆把它列作「现场岗位」，因为主要工作是迎接到访者。

examples.en: An on-site role would be fine if I can cycle there between seminars.
examples.zh: 如果两节研讨课之间能骑车赶过去，「现场岗位」我也能接受。

words.enDefinition: a job carried out mainly away from a central workplace

examples.en: The field-based role involves visiting community gardens rather than spending each day in an office.
examples.zh: 这个「外勤岗位」要走访社区花园，不用天天待在办公室。

examples.en: I saw a field-based role collecting water samples on weekdays with a small team.
examples.zh: 我看到一个「外勤岗位」，工作日和小团队一起采集水样。

words.enDefinition: the place where a job is carried out

examples.en: I checked the work location and found it was on the other side of town.
examples.zh: 我查了「工作地点」，发现它在城市的另一边。

examples.en: The listing names the main work location but mentions an occasional shift elsewhere.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写明了主要「工作地点」，但提到偶尔要去别处上班。

words.enDefinition: work travel that involves staying away overnight

examples.en: The role involves overnight travel twice a term to help run events at other campuses.
examples.zh: 这个岗位每学期有两次「需过夜的出差」，去其他校区协助办活动。

examples.en: I asked how much overnight travel was involved before committing to a full class schedule.
examples.zh: 把一学期的课排满之前，我问了工作有多少次「需过夜的出差」。

words.enDefinition: the typical daytime hours when an office operates

examples.en: The position follows standard business hours, which clash with two of my afternoon classes.
examples.zh: 这个岗位在「常规办公时间」上班，刚好和我两门下午的课冲突。

examples.en: The print shop wants someone who can work standard business hours throughout the summer.
examples.zh: 这家印刷店想找一个整个夏天都能在「常规办公时间」上班的人。

words.enDefinition: working hours that do not change from week to week

examples.en: The role has fixed hours, so I can plan my lectures around the shifts.
examples.zh: 这个岗位有「固定工时」，我可以避开班次来排课。

examples.en: I prefer fixed hours because my evening class always starts at six on Wednesdays.
examples.zh: 我更想要「固定工时」，因为星期三的夜课总是六点开始。

words.enDefinition: working hours that can be adjusted to suit different needs

examples.en: Flexible hours would help me fit a campus job around my weekly lab sessions.
examples.zh: 「弹性工时」能帮我把校内兼职安排在每周实验课以外的时间。

examples.en: The employer offers flexible hours but still expects everyone to attend the Monday meeting.
examples.zh: 雇主提供「弹性工时」，但仍要求所有人参加周一的会议。

words.enDefinition: a block of time when everyone must be working

examples.en: The role has core hours from ten until three, with flexibility on either side.
examples.zh: 这个岗位上午十点到下午三点是「必须在岗的时段」，前后都能灵活安排。

examples.en: I checked whether my Tuesday seminar overlapped with the team's core hours for this position.
examples.zh: 我查了周二的研讨课和这个岗位团队「必须在岗的时段」是否重叠。

words.enDefinition: limited to the weeks when classes are in session

examples.en: The campus café advertised the job as term-time only, leaving the winter break free.
examples.zh: 校内咖啡馆的招聘启事写着「仅学期内工作」，寒假不用上班。

examples.en: I asked whether the role was term-time only because I'll be away in July.
examples.zh: 我问这个岗位是否「仅学期内工作」，因为七月份我不在这儿。

collocations: available on a term-time only basis

words.enDefinition: the ability to work during the evening

examples.en: The theatre requires evening availability on opening nights, even for people who usually work mornings.
examples.zh: 这家剧院要求首演日「晚间可上班」，平时上早班的人也一样。

examples.en: I checked my evening availability before enquiring about the cinema's two weekday shifts.
examples.zh: 打听电影院工作日的两个班次前，我先确认了自己是否「晚间可上班」。

words.enDefinition: a period of work scheduled during daytime hours

examples.en: I could cover a day shift on Friday because my afternoon lecture was cancelled.
examples.zh: 星期五下午的课取消了，我可以顶一个「白班」。

examples.en: The day shift ends early enough for me to catch the last bus home.
examples.zh: 「白班」下班时间够早，我还能赶上回家的末班车。

words.enDefinition: a period of work scheduled mainly during the night

examples.en: The night shift at the residence desk would clash with my early class on Fridays.
examples.zh: 学生宿舍前台要上「夜班」，会影响我周五的早课。

examples.en: I asked whether the night shift ended before the buses started running again.
examples.zh: 我问「夜班」会不会在公交恢复运营之前就下班。

words.enDefinition: a workday divided into separate periods with a long break

examples.en: The café offered me a split shift with three hours off between lunch and dinner.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆给我安排了「分段班次」，午餐和晚餐班之间休息三小时。

examples.en: A split shift would give me enough time to attend my afternoon seminar on campus.
examples.zh: 「分段班次」能给我留出足够的时间去学校上下午的研讨课。

words.enDefinition: work shifts that change regularly from one schedule to another

examples.en: The role includes rotating shifts, so the same person does not always cover weekends.
examples.zh: 这个岗位有「轮换班次」，所以不会总是同一个人周末值班。

examples.en: I couldn't commit to rotating shifts until I got my timetable for next semester.
examples.zh: 在拿到下学期的课表前，我没法确定自己能不能接受「轮换班次」。

words.enDefinition: work scheduled for Saturdays or Sundays

examples.en: The gift shop advertised weekend work, which would fit around my classes during the week.
examples.zh: 礼品店在招「周末工作」的人，这样不会和我平时的课冲突。

examples.en: I can do weekend work as long as I have enough notice to move things around.
examples.zh: 只要提前告诉我，让我有时间调整安排，我就能做「周末工作」。

words.enDefinition: a period when someone must be ready to respond if needed

examples.en: The residence manager said an on-call shift meant keeping my phone close throughout the night.
examples.zh: 宿舍经理说，「待命班次」意味着整夜都得把手机放在身边。

examples.en: I can't take an on-call shift that evening because I'll be on a train.
examples.zh: 那天晚上我要坐火车，没法接「待命班次」。

words.enDefinition: a minimum amount of work time the employer commits to providing

examples.en: The advert mentioned guaranteed hours, which would make it easier to budget for rent.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到有「保证安排的工时」，这样我更容易做房租预算。

examples.en: I asked if guaranteed hours were included because I couldn't rely on occasional shifts.
examples.zh: 我问有没有「保证安排的工时」，因为我不能只靠偶尔排个班。

words.enDefinition: extra hours that are only needed from time to time

examples.en: The role requires occasional overtime when visiting speakers stay late after a lecture.
examples.zh: 外来讲者讲完课后留到很晚时，这个岗位需要「偶尔加班」。

examples.en: I could manage occasional overtime as long as it didn't clash with my evening classes.
examples.zh: 只要不和夜课冲突，我可以接受「偶尔加班」。

words.enDefinition: a job arrangement that starts without a waiting period

examples.en: The ad offered an immediate start, but my exams wouldn't finish until next week.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着可以「立即上岗」，但我下周才考完试。

examples.en: I told the gallery I was available for an immediate start once classes finished.
examples.zh: 我跟美术馆说，课程一结束我就能「立即上岗」。

words.enDefinition: the schedule can be settled by discussion

examples.en: The advert says the hours are negotiable, so I might be able to fit it around lectures.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着「工作时间可协商」，我或许能把上班时间安排在课外。

examples.en: The hours are negotiable, but the manager needs someone there every Friday morning.
examples.zh: 「工作时间可协商」，不过经理需要每周五上午都有人在场。

collocations: ask whether the hours are negotiable

words.enDefinition: a condition every suitable applicant needs to meet

examples.en: Weekend availability was an essential criterion, so I checked the dates of my field trips.
examples.zh: 周末能上班是「必备条件」，所以我查了一下实地考察的日期。

examples.en: The museum listed written English as an essential criterion for answering emails from visitors.
examples.zh: 博物馆把书面英语列为「必备条件」，因为这份工作要回复来访者的邮件。

collocations: list something as an essential criterion

words.enDefinition: a condition that is preferred but not required

examples.en: Theatre experience was a desirable criterion, so I applied even though I'd never worked backstage.
examples.zh: 剧院工作经验是「优先考虑的条件」，所以虽然没在后台工作过，我还是申请了。

examples.en: The listing treated spreadsheet knowledge as a desirable criterion for the weekend reception role.
examples.zh: 招聘启事把会用电子表格列为周末接待岗「优先考虑的条件」。

collocations: treat something as a desirable criterion

words.enDefinition: the lowest level of credentials or experience an employer will accept

examples.en: I read the minimum qualifications carefully because my diploma was earned in another country.
examples.zh: 我的文凭是在另一个国家拿的，所以我仔细读了「最低任职资格」。

examples.en: The minimum qualifications include a childcare certificate and previous work with young children.
examples.zh: 「最低任职资格」包括持有幼儿照护证书，以及有和幼儿共事的经验。

words.enDefinition: abilities an employer expects every suitable applicant to have

examples.en: I had most of the required skills, but the spreadsheet test was new to me.
examples.zh: 「必备技能」我大多具备，只是没做过电子表格测试。

examples.en: The required skills include using a till and speaking clearly with people over the phone.
examples.zh: 「必备技能」包括会用收银机，以及能在电话里和人清楚地沟通。

words.enDefinition: past work or activities that relate to the role

examples.en: I asked whether my campus radio work counted as relevant experience for the role.
examples.zh: 我问我在校园电台做过的事算不算这个岗位的「相关经历」。

examples.en: The shop accepts relevant experience from volunteering as well as from previous paid jobs.
examples.zh: 这家商店认可从志愿服务和以往有薪工作中积累的「相关经历」。

words.enDefinition: experience accepted in place of a stated credential or requirement

examples.en: The listing says the lab accepts equivalent experience if you don't have the named certificate.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着，如果没有列出的证书，实验室也认可「可替代资质的经验」。

examples.en: I asked whether two years in the campus workshop would count as equivalent experience.
examples.zh: 我问在学校工坊做两年算不算「可替代资质的经验」。

words.enDefinition: within an area of study or work connected to the role

examples.en: The ad asks for a diploma in design or in a related field.
examples.zh: 招聘启事要求持有设计专业或「相关领域的」文凭。

examples.en: I checked whether volunteering in a related field would be enough for the position.
examples.zh: 我查了在「相关领域」做过志愿者是否足以申请这个岗位。

collocations: a degree in a related field

words.enDefinition: the number of years spent doing a particular kind of work

examples.en: The job asks for two years of experience, so I checked whether placements count.
examples.zh: 这份工作要求「两年工作经验」，所以我查了一下实习算不算。

examples.en: The ad asks for several years of experience supervising staff in a busy shop.
examples.zh: 招聘启事要求有「数年工作经验」，具体是在繁忙的商店里带员工。

collocations: at least two years of experience

words.enDefinition: an ability supported by actual examples or evidence

examples.en: The listing asks for demonstrated ability to organize events, even if they were small.
examples.zh: 招聘启事要求「证明自己有组织活动的能力」，办过小型活动也算。

examples.en: The work calls for demonstrated ability to explain complex material to a general audience.
examples.zh: 这份工作要求「证明自己有向普通听众解释复杂材料的能力」。

words.enDefinition: knowledge gained by actually doing the work yourself

examples.en: The workshop wants hands-on experience with basic tools, rather than just knowledge from lectures.
examples.zh: 工坊看重使用基础工具的「动手实践经验」，光有课堂知识还不够。

examples.en: My course gave me hands-on experience with recording equipment, which the listing specifically mentioned.
examples.zh: 课程让我积累了操作录音设备的「动手实践经验」，招聘启事特意提到这一点。

words.enDefinition: experience working in a particular industry

examples.en: The audio company asks for industry experience even though the position is listed as junior.
examples.zh: 尽管岗位写的是初级，这家音频公司还是要求有「行业工作经验」。

examples.en: I checked whether my time with a local publisher counted as industry experience.
examples.zh: 我查了一下，在本地出版社工作的那段时间算不算「行业工作经验」。

words.enDefinition: experience overseeing the work of other people

examples.en: The café asks for supervisory experience because the person will lead the evening team.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆要求有「带人管理经验」，因为这个人要带晚班团队。

examples.en: I asked if organizing shifts for student volunteers counted as supervisory experience for the role.
examples.zh: 我问给学生志愿者排班算不算这个岗位要求的「带人管理经验」。

words.enDefinition: experience doing work that involves direct contact with customers

examples.en: The box office job asks for customer-facing experience, so my time in retail was relevant.
examples.zh: 售票处的工作要求有「直接接待顾客的经验」，因此我做零售的经历正用得上。

examples.en: I gained customer-facing experience when I helped visitors at the university's open day.
examples.zh: 学校开放日我帮忙接待来访者，积累了「直接接待顾客的经验」。

words.enDefinition: a formal qualification for work in a particular profession

examples.en: The listing asks for a professional qualification, so I looked up the named credential.
examples.zh: 招聘启事要求有「职业资格」，我就去查了它点名的那项资质。

examples.en: I asked if my professional qualification from home would be relevant to this role.
examples.zh: 我问自己在老家取得的「职业资格」是否适用于这个岗位。

words.enDefinition: official registration with a body that oversees a profession

examples.en: The clinic's listing asks for current professional registration with the body named in the advert.
examples.zh: 这家诊所的招聘启事要求在指定机构办理「执业注册」，而且注册须在有效期内。

examples.en: I contacted the employer to clarify which professional registration they expected for the position.
examples.zh: 我联系了雇主，想弄清这个岗位要求哪一种「执业注册」。

words.enDefinition: a credential accepted as comparable to the one requested

examples.en: I asked whether my certificate counted as an equivalent qualification for the library position.
examples.zh: 我问我的证书算不算图书馆岗位要求的「同等资格」。

examples.en: The advert lists a local diploma or an equivalent qualification from another country.
examples.zh: 招聘启事列出了本地文凭，或是在其他国家取得的「同等资格」。

words.enDefinition: someone who finished their studies a short time ago

examples.en: As a recent graduate, I wanted a job that still offered some training.
examples.zh: 作为「刚毕业的人」，我想找一份还能提供一些培训的工作。

examples.en: The publisher is looking for a recent graduate who is interested in editing textbooks.
examples.zh: 出版社想找个对教材编辑有兴趣的「刚毕业的人」。

collocations: a role for a recent graduate

words.enDefinition: previous work experience is not a condition for applying

examples.en: The sign said 'No experience required,' so I asked about the weekend café shifts.
examples.zh: 告示写着「无需工作经验」，所以我去问了咖啡馆周末班的情况。

examples.en: I applied because the advert said 'No experience required' and classes had just ended.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着「无需工作经验」，我又刚上完课，就去申请了。

collocations: a sign saying no experience required
an ad marked no experience required
a role advertised with no experience required

words.enDefinition: no official credential is needed to apply

examples.en: The poster said 'No formal qualifications required,' but new staff had to complete training.
examples.zh: 海报写着「无需正式资质」，但新员工必须完成培训。

examples.en: The advert says 'No formal qualifications required,' so I asked which skills they valued.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着「无需正式资质」，所以我问他们看重哪些技能。

collocations: advertised with no formal qualifications required
roles with no formal qualifications required
listed as no formal qualifications required

words.enDefinition: official permission to access protected places or information after checks

examples.en: The archive listing mentions security clearance for staff who access the restricted collection.
examples.zh: 档案馆的招聘启事提到，接触限制阅览馆藏的员工需要「安全审查许可」。

examples.en: I asked when security clearance would be checked for the role at the airport.
examples.zh: 我问机场的这个岗位会在什么时候核验「安全审查许可」。

words.enDefinition: the ability to use a vehicle when needed

examples.en: The fieldwork assistant role requires access to a vehicle for occasional visits outside town.
examples.zh: 野外工作助理偶尔要去城外走访，因此要求「有车可用」。

examples.en: I asked whether I needed access to a vehicle every day or just on Fridays.
examples.zh: 我问是每天都得「有车可用」，还是只需要周五用车。

words.zhGloss: 能实际运用的基础知识
words.enDefinition: enough understanding of something to use it for everyday tasks
acceptedZhAnswers: 能实际运用的基础知识

examples.en: The role asks for a working knowledge of spreadsheets so you can update simple records.
examples.zh: 这个岗位要求「懂基本的电子表格操作」，能更新简单的记录。

examples.en: I have a working knowledge of photo editing from helping with the student newsletter.
examples.zh: 我帮学生通讯做过编辑，「懂基本的照片编辑操作」。

collocations: a working knowledge of office software
require a working knowledge of something

words.enDefinition: able to use a skill or tool well

examples.en: The editor wants someone proficient in design software who can make changes without help.
examples.zh: 编辑想找一个「熟练掌握设计软件」的人，可以独立修改文件。

examples.en: I checked what they meant by proficient in Excel before deciding whether to apply.
examples.zh: 决定是否申请前，我确认了他们要求的「熟练掌握 Excel」具体指什么。

words.enDefinition: the ability to speak or use a language smoothly

examples.en: The campus tour job requires fluency in English because you'll answer visitors' questions as you walk.
examples.zh: 校园导览岗位要求「流利使用英语」，因为你要边走边回答来访者的问题。

examples.en: The notice says fluency in French is helpful for greeting visitors from the partner university.
examples.zh: 启事上说，「流利使用法语」有助于接待合作院校的访客。

words.enDefinition: the ability to share information clearly in writing

examples.en: The role calls for written communication skills because the assistant answers most questions by email.
examples.zh: 岗位要求有「书面沟通能力」，因为助理主要通过邮件回答问题。

examples.en: The listing mentions written communication skills for turning meeting notes into short updates.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到要有「书面沟通能力」，能把会议笔记整理成简短的进展说明。

words.enDefinition: the ability to explain ideas and understand others in conversation

examples.en: The tour guide role needs verbal communication skills to explain directions in a busy building.
examples.zh: 导览岗位需要「口头沟通能力」，以便在繁忙的大楼里把路线讲清楚。

examples.en: The ad mentions verbal communication skills because staff often talk to families over the phone.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到「口头沟通能力」，因为员工经常要在电话里和家属沟通。

words.enDefinition: the ability to interact effectively with other people

examples.en: The role needs interpersonal skills because students often arrive at the desk feeling confused.
examples.zh: 这个岗位需要「人际交往能力」，因为学生到前台时经常还弄不清状况。

examples.en: I highlighted the line about interpersonal skills when I was reading the residence job description.
examples.zh: 我读宿舍岗位说明时，标出了关于「人际交往能力」的那一行。

words.enDefinition: the ability to identify difficulties and find workable solutions

examples.en: The ad asks for problem-solving skills because equipment sometimes fails during student events.
examples.zh: 招聘启事要求有「解决问题的能力」，因为学生活动期间设备有时会出故障。

examples.en: The role mentions problem-solving skills for helping visitors when rooms or bookings change unexpectedly.
examples.zh: 岗位提到要有「解决问题的能力」，遇到房间或预订临时变动时能帮到来访者。

words.enDefinition: the ability to use common computers and software confidently

examples.en: The job asks for computer literacy because orders are entered on a desktop computer.
examples.zh: 这份工作需要「基本计算机使用能力」，因为订单要在台式电脑上录入。

examples.en: I checked whether computer literacy meant using specialized programs or just everyday office software.
examples.zh: 我查了一下，「基本计算机使用能力」是指会用专业程序，还是会用常用办公软件就行。

words.enDefinition: tasks somebody does regularly as part of a job

examples.en: The day-to-day duties include opening the study room and checking who has booked it.
examples.zh: 「日常工作职责」包括开放自习室，以及查看预订人是谁。

examples.en: I asked what the day-to-day duties looked like when there were no events booked.
examples.zh: 我问没有活动预订的时候，「日常工作职责」具体是什么。

words.enDefinition: the most important things a worker is expected to do

examples.en: One of the key responsibilities is making sure hired equipment comes back in good condition.
examples.zh: 「主要职责」之一是确保租出去的设备完好归还。

examples.en: The advert lists the key responsibilities on the first page under the position title.
examples.zh: 招聘启事在第一页的职位名称下面列出了「主要职责」。

words.enDefinition: additional tasks that a supervisor may assign as needed

examples.en: The listing says other duties as assigned, so I asked what else staff help with.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着「另有交办事项」，所以我问员工通常还要帮忙做什么。

examples.en: The phrase other duties as assigned appeared just after the list of regular tasks.
examples.zh: 常规任务清单后面紧跟着「另有交办事项」几个字。

collocations: a section on other duties as assigned

words.enDefinition: be directly accountable to a particular manager or supervisor

examples.en: The listing says I'll report directly to the museum manager instead of the events coordinator.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着，我会「直接向博物馆经理汇报」，不是向活动协调员汇报。

examples.en: Our student assistants report directly to the head librarian on the days they work.
examples.zh: 学生助理在上班的日子「直接向图书馆馆长汇报」。

collocations: report directly to the team lead

words.enDefinition: employees who report to a particular manager without anyone in between

examples.en: The coordinator role has three direct reports who help run events across different campuses.
examples.zh: 协调员岗位有三名「直属下属」，协助组织各校区的活动。

examples.en: The listing specified that the assistant manager would have no direct reports at first.
examples.zh: 招聘启事明确写着，副经理刚开始没有「直属下属」。

words.enDefinition: oversee the work of a group of employees

examples.en: The role asks you to supervise a team of student workers in the equipment room.
examples.zh: 这个岗位要求在器材室「管理一支学生员工团队」。

examples.en: I was surprised that the weekend manager had to supervise a team of twelve.
examples.zh: 我没想到周末值班经理要「管理一支团队」，而且有十二个人。

collocations: train someone to supervise a team

words.enDefinition: carry out tasks without regular help or supervision

examples.en: The app developer must work independently while the rest of the team is abroad.
examples.zh: 其他团队成员都在国外时，应用开发人员必须「独立工作」。

examples.en: The role lets me work independently once I understand how the archive is organized.
examples.zh: 等我弄清档案是怎么整理的，这个岗位就可以「独立工作」了。

words.enDefinition: perform tasks in stressful or demanding conditions

examples.en: People in the ticket office sometimes work under pressure when several events start together.
examples.zh: 几场活动同时开始时，售票处的人有时要「在压力下工作」。

examples.en: The description says you'll work under pressure on Fridays when the café is busiest.
examples.zh: 岗位说明写着，星期五咖啡馆最忙，你要「在压力下工作」。

collocations: work under pressure in a busy setting

words.enDefinition: the habit of noticing and checking small important details

examples.en: The archive asks for attention to detail because missing labels can make items hard to find.
examples.zh: 档案馆要求「注重细节」，因为少一张标签就可能很难找到物品。

examples.en: The description stresses attention to detail when checking names on event bookings each morning.
examples.zh: 岗位说明强调，每天早上核对活动预订上的姓名时要「注重细节」。

words.enDefinition: finish work on time when little time is available

examples.en: The student newspaper needs assistants who can meet tight deadlines before each issue goes out.
examples.zh: 学生报社需要能在每期发行前「在紧迫期限内完成工作」的助理。

examples.en: The role requires you to meet tight deadlines when last-minute changes come in from lecturers.
examples.zh: 这个岗位要求在讲师临时提出修改时，也能「在紧迫期限内完成」。

collocations: work together to meet tight deadlines
under pressure to meet tight deadlines

words.enDefinition: decide what to do first when important tasks compete for time

examples.en: The assistant must manage competing priorities when several lecturers ask for help at once.
examples.zh: 好几位讲师同时求助时，助理必须「分清这些要务的先后顺序」。

examples.en: I asked how the team would help me manage competing priorities during the busy weeks.
examples.zh: 我问最忙的那几个星期，团队会怎样帮我「排定多项要务的先后顺序」。

words.enDefinition: someone who takes initiative without waiting for instructions

examples.en: The ad asks for a self-starter who can spot what needs doing without reminders.
examples.zh: 招聘启事要找「能主动开展工作的人」，不用提醒就能看出什么事该做。

examples.en: The coffee cart needs a self-starter because no supervisor is there in the mornings.
examples.zh: 咖啡餐车早上没有主管在场，所以需要「能主动开展工作的人」。

words.enDefinition: open to gaining new skills or knowledge

examples.en: The shop wants someone willing to learn how to repair zips and replace buttons.
examples.zh: 这家店要找一个「愿意学习」怎么修拉链、换纽扣的人。

examples.en: You don't need to know the software yet if you're willing to learn it.
examples.zh: 你现在不用会用这个软件，只要「愿意学」就行。

collocations: someone who is willing to learn

words.enDefinition: help with the routine paperwork and organization of an office

examples.en: The role involves administrative support for a small department that runs courses in the evenings.
examples.zh: 这个岗位为一个开设夜间课程的小院系提供「行政事务支持」。

examples.en: I asked what administrative support meant in a department where most forms are online.
examples.zh: 这个院系的大部分表格都在线上，所以我问「行政事务支持」具体指什么。

words.enDefinition: arrange timing so that different people's plans work together

examples.en: The assistant will coordinate schedules for visiting speakers who come from several different campuses.
examples.zh: 助理要为来自不同校区的外来讲者「协调日程」。

examples.en: The department wants someone to coordinate schedules when two tutorials share the same classroom.
examples.zh: 两个辅导课共用一间教室，院系想找个人来「协调日程」。

words.enDefinition: keep information written down correctly and up to date

examples.en: The residence receptionist must maintain accurate records of which students are holding borrowed keys.
examples.zh: 宿舍前台必须「准确记录」哪些学生借走了钥匙。

examples.en: Applicants should be able to maintain accurate records even when the office is very busy.
examples.zh: 即便办公室很忙，申请人也应该有能力「确保记录准确」。

collocations: maintain accurate records for a team

words.enDefinition: respond to questions or requests for information

examples.en: The job involves being at reception to handle enquiries from visitors during the mornings.
examples.zh: 这份工作上午要在前台「处理来访者的咨询」。

examples.en: The museum needs someone who can handle enquiries about group bookings over the phone.
examples.zh: 博物馆需要有人能通过电话「处理团体预订方面的咨询」。

words.enDefinition: carry out the steps needed to fulfill customer orders

examples.en: The bookshop needs someone to process orders for textbooks before the first week of term.
examples.zh: 书店需要有人在学期第一周前「处理教材订单」。

examples.en: I asked whether I would process orders or mainly help customers on the shop floor.
examples.zh: 我问自己是要「处理订单」，还是主要在店里接待顾客。

words.enDefinition: work with information that must stay private

examples.en: The office needs someone who can handle confidential information when answering questions about student records.
examples.zh: 办公室需要有人在回答学籍记录相关问题时，能妥善「处理保密信息」。

examples.en: The ad mentions that assistants handle confidential information while preparing documents for private meetings.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到，助理为非公开会议准备材料时会「处理保密信息」。

words.enDefinition: stay in contact with someone to coordinate shared work

examples.en: The assistant will liaise with security to arrange access for groups visiting after hours.
examples.zh: 助理会「与安保人员联络协调」，安排下班后到访的团体进场。

examples.en: I asked how often I'd liaise with staff from the other campus during term.
examples.zh: 我问学期内多久需要「与另一个校区的员工联络协调」一次。

collocations: liaise with members of the public

words.enDefinition: replacing goods that have been sold or used up

examples.en: The early shift is mainly stock replenishment before customers arrive at the campus shop.
examples.zh: 早班主要是在顾客到校内商店之前「补货」。

examples.en: The advert mentions stock replenishment as well as answering questions on the shop floor.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到，除了在店里回答顾客的问题，还要「补货」。

words.enDefinition: putting information into a computer system or database

examples.en: The job involves data entry for a project that collects feedback from first-year students.
examples.zh: 这份工作涉及一个收集大一学生反馈的项目，需要做「数据录入」。

examples.en: I asked how much data entry was involved before applying for the records assistant role.
examples.zh: 申请档案助理岗位前，我问了有多少「数据录入」工作。

words.enDefinition: lifting, carrying, or moving objects using physical effort

examples.en: The advert mentions manual handling because the job includes moving boxes of donated books.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到有「人工搬运」，因为这份工作要挪装着捐赠书籍的箱子。

examples.en: I asked whether the manual handling duties were mainly in the storeroom or at events.
examples.zh: 我问「人工搬运」主要是在仓库里，还是在活动现场做。

words.enDefinition: remaining on your feet for a long period

examples.en: The listing mentions prolonged standing because ushers stay near the theatre doors during performances.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到要「长时间站立」，因为演出期间引座员要守在剧院门口附近。

examples.en: The ticket counter listing mentions prolonged standing, so I asked how long shifts lasted.
examples.zh: 售票柜台的招聘启事提到要「长时间站立」，所以我问了每个班次有多长。

words.enDefinition: a job an organization has introduced for the first time

examples.en: The university advertised a newly created role to help students find local volunteering projects.
examples.zh: 学校招聘一个「新设岗位」，负责帮学生找本地志愿服务项目。

examples.en: I read the duties carefully because it was a newly created role without a predecessor.
examples.zh: 这是个「新设岗位」，此前没人做过，所以我认真读了岗位职责。

collocations: take on a newly created role
a newly created role in the team

words.enDefinition: working alone without other staff nearby

examples.en: The listing mentioned lone working because only one attendant is scheduled after eight at night.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到要「独自值守」，因为晚上八点后只安排一名工作人员。

examples.en: I asked whether lone working was part of opening the building on Saturday mornings.
examples.zh: 我问周六早上去开楼门时是不是要「独自值守」。

words.enDefinition: very little guidance or monitoring from a supervisor

examples.en: The notice says assistants work with minimal supervision once they know the booking system.
examples.zh: 通知上写着，助理熟悉预约系统后，工作「很少需要督导」。

examples.en: I asked if minimal supervision meant the manager normally worked in a different building.
examples.zh: 我问「很少需要督导」是不是意味着经理平时在另一栋楼里上班。

words.enDefinition: a job that involves working across different teams or functions

examples.en: I applied for a cross-functional role that links the training team with the library.
examples.zh: 我申请了一个连接培训团队和图书馆的「跨职能岗位」。

examples.en: The cross-functional role involves working with both the fundraising team and the events team.
examples.zh: 这个「跨职能岗位」要同时和筹款团队、活动团队合作。

words.enDefinition: work periods that somebody else cannot take

examples.en: The casual role is mainly to cover shifts when other café staff are away.
examples.zh: 这个临时岗位主要是在咖啡馆其他员工不在时「顶班」。

examples.en: I can cover shifts at the library on Thursdays because my classes finish early.
examples.zh: 我周四的课结束得早，可以去图书馆「顶班」。

words.enDefinition: the physical effort or activity a job involves

examples.en: The physical demands are listed separately from the training required for the theatre role.
examples.zh: 剧院岗位把「体力要求」和必需的培训分开列出。

examples.en: I asked about the physical demands before applying for the summer warehouse position.
examples.zh: 申请暑期仓库岗位前，我先问了有什么「体力要求」。

collocations: the physical demands of the role

words.enDefinition: a driving history without relevant violations or serious incidents

examples.en: The delivery listing asks for a clean driving record, so I checked what they meant.
examples.zh: 送货岗位的招聘启事要求「无不良驾驶记录」，所以我去问了具体指什么。

examples.en: I asked how the employer defined a clean driving record before filling in the form.
examples.zh: 填表前，我问雇主怎么定义「无不良驾驶记录」。

collocations: show proof of a clean driving record

words.enDefinition: the amount paid for one hour of work

examples.en: The listing gives an hourly rate for the café shifts instead of an annual salary.
examples.zh: 招聘启事给咖啡馆的班次标了「时薪」，用的不是年薪。

examples.en: I checked whether the hourly rate was the same for weekend and weekday shifts.
examples.zh: 我查了周末班和工作日班的「时薪」是否一样。

words.enDefinition: the span between the lowest and highest salaries listed for a job

examples.en: The salary range appears near the bottom of the listing, just above the benefits.
examples.zh: 「薪资范围」在招聘启事靠下的位置，就在福利说明上面。

examples.en: I asked whether the salary range applied to the part-time version of the role.
examples.zh: 我问这个「薪资范围」是否也适用于兼职岗位。

words.enDefinition: set at a level that reflects someone's experience

examples.en: The listing says pay is commensurate with experience, but it doesn't give a figure.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着薪酬「与经验相匹配」，但没给具体数字。

examples.en: We discussed what pay commensurate with experience meant for applicants who were changing careers.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了对转行求职的人来说，薪酬「与经验相匹配」具体是什么意思。

words.enDefinition: pay presented as matching or exceeding pay for similar jobs

examples.en: The advert promises a competitive salary without giving an amount for the weekend role.
examples.zh: 招聘启事说周末岗位提供「有竞争力的薪资」，但没写具体金额。

examples.en: I wanted to know what a competitive salary meant for an assistant in this area.
examples.zh: 我想了解在这一带，助理拿多少才算「有竞争力的薪资」。

collocations: a competitive salary for the role

words.enDefinition: pay equal to one and a half times the usual rate

examples.en: The theatre listing says staff earn time and a half when they cover certain holidays.
examples.zh: 这家剧院的招聘启事写着，员工在某些节假日顶班能拿「一点五倍工资」。

examples.en: I asked which shifts qualified for time and a half at the campus shop.
examples.zh: 我问校内商店哪些班次可拿「一点五倍工资」。

words.enDefinition: sales-based pay with no stated maximum amount

examples.en: The listing offers uncapped commission, so I asked how the basic hourly pay worked.
examples.zh: 招聘启事说「提成上不封顶」，于是我问基本时薪怎么算。

examples.en: The shop advertises uncapped commission for staff who help customers choose broadband packages.
examples.zh: 这家店在招聘帮助顾客选择宽带套餐的员工，注明「提成上不封顶」。

words.enDefinition: extra pay based on how well someone does their job

examples.en: The advert mentions a performance bonus but doesn't say how success is measured.
examples.zh: 招聘启事说有「绩效奖金」，但没写表现怎么评估。

examples.en: I asked whether part-time staff could also earn a performance bonus at the end of term.
examples.zh: 我问兼职人员期末是否也能拿到「绩效奖金」。

words.enDefinition: instruction for a job during time for which you are paid

examples.en: The campus shop offers paid training before new staff start working at the till.
examples.zh: 新员工开始做收银之前，学校商店提供「带薪培训」。

examples.en: I checked the dates of the paid training because I had two exams that week.
examples.zh: 我查了「带薪培训」的日期，因为那一周有两场考试。

words.enDefinition: help from an employer with the cost of courses

examples.en: The hospital lists tuition assistance for employees taking courses related to their current roles.
examples.zh: 医院的招聘启事写着，员工上和目前岗位相关的课可获「雇主学费补助」。

examples.en: I asked whether the tuition assistance covered short courses as well as degree programs.
examples.zh: 我问短期课程是否也能获得「雇主学费补助」，还是只有学位课程才行。

words.enDefinition: a reduced price an employer offers to its staff

examples.en: The bookshop offers an employee discount that I could use to buy course books.
examples.zh: 书店有「员工折扣」，我买课程用书时也能用。

examples.en: I asked whether the employee discount also applied to items ordered online for collection.
examples.zh: 我问网上订购后到店自取的商品也能不能用「员工折扣」。

words.enDefinition: a meal provided for people working at a business

examples.en: The restaurant offers a staff meal on evenings when you work past closing time.
examples.zh: 晚上上班超过打烊时间，餐厅会提供一份「员工餐」。

examples.en: I checked whether the staff meal was available before or after the dinner shift.
examples.zh: 我查了一下「员工餐」是在晚餐班之前吃，还是下班后吃。

words.enDefinition: the employer supplies the clothing worn for the job

examples.en: The listing says 'Uniform provided,' so I asked how shoe sizes were handled.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着「提供工作制服」，所以我问工作鞋的尺码怎么选。

examples.en: I noticed 'Uniform provided' at the bottom of the ad for the museum shop.
examples.zh: 我在博物馆商店的招聘启事底部看到「提供工作制服」。

words.enDefinition: repayment of expenses from travel connected with work

examples.en: The theatre offers travel reimbursement when staff have to visit its other sites.
examples.zh: 员工需要去其他场地时，剧院提供「出行费用报销」。

examples.en: I asked if travel reimbursement covered train tickets to the company's training centre.
examples.zh: 我问去公司培训中心的火车票能不能算在「出行费用报销」里。

words.enDefinition: the amount of annual leave a worker is allowed

examples.en: I checked the annual leave entitlement before deciding whether the longer contract suited me.
examples.zh: 在决定较长的合同适不适合我之前，我查了「年假额度」。

examples.en: The employer listed the annual leave entitlement separately for full-time and part-time staff.
examples.zh: 雇主分开列出了全职和兼职人员的「年假额度」。

collocations: the annual leave entitlement for part-time staff

words.enDefinition: chances to develop knowledge and skills for your work

examples.en: The department advertises professional development opportunities such as workshops on interviewing research participants.
examples.zh: 院系的招聘启事提到有「职业能力提升机会」，比如有关研究访谈的工作坊。

examples.en: I asked what professional development opportunities would be available to a new archive assistant.
examples.zh: 我问刚入职的档案助理可以获得哪些「职业能力提升机会」。

words.enDefinition: chances to move into roles with more responsibility

examples.en: The listing mentioned opportunities for advancement from weekend assistant to a role with supervisory duties.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到有「晋升机会」，可从周末助理升到带人的岗位。

examples.en: I asked about opportunities for advancement because I'd like to stay after graduation.
examples.zh: 我想毕业后继续做，所以问了有没有「晋升机会」。

words.enDefinition: tools or devices supplied by an employer for work

examples.en: The remote role includes company-provided equipment, so I wouldn't need to use my own laptop.
examples.zh: 这个远程岗位有「公司提供的设备」，所以我不用自己的笔记本电脑。

examples.en: I checked whether company-provided equipment included a headset for answering calls from home.
examples.zh: 我查了「公司提供的设备」里有没有用于在家接电话的耳麦。

words.enDefinition: employment benefits that help cover health-related needs or costs

examples.en: The advert mentions health benefits and links to a page explaining what they include.
examples.zh: 招聘启事提到有「员工健康福利」，还附了个链接说明包括哪些项目。

examples.en: I asked whether health benefits were available to staff working only on weekends.
examples.zh: 我问只在周末上班的员工能否享受「员工健康福利」。

words.enDefinition: the set of non-wage benefits offered with a job

examples.en: The listing outlines a benefits package that includes a discounted bus pass and paid leave.
examples.zh: 招聘启事概述了「综合福利待遇」，其中有公交月票折扣和带薪假。

examples.en: I checked the benefits package because the employer and the agency described it differently.
examples.zh: 雇主和中介说法不一样，所以我仔细读了「综合福利待遇」。

words.enDefinition: short periods off during a shift that still count as paid time

examples.en: The role description says paid breaks are included in the hours shown on the schedule.
examples.zh: 岗位说明写着，排班表上的工时包含「带薪休息时间」。

examples.en: I asked about paid breaks because some shifts would last through the whole afternoon.
examples.zh: 我问了有没有「带薪休息时间」，因为有些班要上整个下午。

words.enDefinition: a pause during a shift for which you are not paid

examples.en: The schedule has an unpaid break between the morning session and the afternoon workshop.
examples.zh: 早上的活动和下午的工作坊之间，排班表安排了「不计薪的休息时间」。

examples.en: I checked whether the unpaid break would be included in the total hours shown.
examples.zh: 我查了「不计薪的休息时间」是否会算在显示的总工时里。

words.enDefinition: working times or amounts that change from week to week

examples.en: The advert lists variable hours because the number of events changes from week to week.
examples.zh: 招聘启事注明「工时不固定」，因为每周活动的数量不同。

examples.en: I could work variable hours during the break, but my term schedule is fixed.
examples.zh: 假期我可以接受「不固定的工时」，但我学期内的时间是固定的。

words.enDefinition: work that begins comparatively early in the day

examples.en: The bakery job has an early start on Mondays to prepare orders for local shops.
examples.zh: 面包店的工作星期一「很早就开始」，要给本地商店准备订单。

examples.en: I checked whether there was a bus because the role involves an early start.
examples.zh: 这个岗位要「很早开始上班」，所以我查了那个点有没有公交。

collocations: be ready for an early start

words.enDefinition: the usual arrangement of the days or hours someone works

examples.en: The working pattern includes short shifts on weekdays and a longer shift every other Saturday.
examples.zh: 「工作时间安排」是工作日上短班，每隔一周的周六上一个长班。

examples.en: I asked if my working pattern could change when the new term began.
examples.zh: 我问新学期开始后，自己的「工作时间安排」能不能调整。

words.enDefinition: at several locations used by the same organization

examples.en: The role involves working across multiple sites, so I checked how far apart they were.
examples.zh: 这个岗位要「在多个工作地点」上班，所以我查了它们相距多远。

examples.en: The technician provides support across multiple sites, including a small workshop outside the city.
examples.zh: 技术员「在多个工作地点」提供支持，包括城外一间小工坊。

words.enDefinition: do your job on officially recognized holidays

examples.en: The listing asks whether student guides can work on public holidays during the summer.
examples.zh: 招聘启事询问学生导览员夏天能否「在公共假日上班」。

examples.en: I asked how often front desk staff would need to work on public holidays.
examples.zh: 我问前台员工多久要「在公共假日上班」一次。

collocations: required to work on public holidays
available to work on public holidays
asked to work on public holidays

words.enDefinition: restricted to Monday through Friday of a usual week

examples.en: The position was listed as weekdays only, so I could keep coaching on Saturdays.
examples.zh: 招聘启事写着「仅限工作日」，我就能继续在周六当教练。

examples.en: I can work weekdays only once the university sports season starts again next month.
examples.zh: 学校的运动赛季下个月重新开始后，我就「只能在工作日上班」了。

words.enDefinition: work trips that take place only from time to time

examples.en: The research role includes occasional travel to schools where the team collects survey responses.
examples.zh: 这个研究岗位要「偶尔出差」，去团队收集问卷的学校。

examples.en: I asked how much notice I'd get for occasional travel once classes resumed.
examples.zh: 我问复课后需要「偶尔出差」时，会提前多久通知我。
